cultural.vision_reason: This is a wooden Qur'anic writing board (allo) with leather-bound handle, used for Islamic religious education—a well-attested item among Hausa Muslim communities in Niger/Nigeria for teaching Qur'anic recitation and writing. It is a genuine ritual/religious object, though not a mask; category should be corrected.

physical.title: qur'an-board
physical.summary: Qur'an-board (allo) made of wood, rectangular, with curved handle at top. Semi-circular section cut from board at bottom to create two feet. Neck of handle bound with strips of green- and yellow-dyed leather twisted together; head of handle covered with red-dyed leather decorated with painted geometric patterns in black stain. Yellow-dyed tassels at either corner with green-dyed knots. Red-dyed leather carrying strap attached to top of handle and decorated with double wavy lines in black stain. Board inscribed on front and back with passages from the Qur'an in Arabic script. The main lettering is in brown ink with diacriticals and vowels in faded red ink. Text surrounded by elaborate geometric patterns painted in brown, yellow and faded red inks.
